Let \(x=-t\), \(0\le t\le 3\). The condition \(P(-3)=1\) gives
\[
1-3+\frac92-27a+81b=1,
\]
so
\[
a=3b+\frac1{18}.
\]
Then
\[
P(-t)-1=-t+\frac{t^2}{2}-\left(3b+\frac1{18}\right)t^3+bt^4
=t(t-3)\left(bt^2-\frac t{18}+\frac13\right).
\]
For the maximizing polynomial found below, \(0<b<1/27\). Hence
\[
bt^2-\frac t{18}+\frac13>0
\]
on \([0,3]\), and also
\[
t(3-t)\left(bt^2-\frac t{18}+\frac13\right)
\le \frac94\cdot \frac12<2,
\]
so the real-axis constraint is satisfied.

Now put \(s=y^2\). Since
\[
P(iy)=1-\frac{s}{2}+bs^2+i\left(y-ay^{{3}}\right),
\]
we get
\[
|P(iy)|^2-1
=s^2\left(b^2s^2+\left(a^2-b\right)s+\frac14+2b-2a\right).
\]
Using \(a=3b+\frac1{18}\),
\[
|P(iy)|^2-1
=s^2\left[
b^2s^2+\frac{(54b-1)^2}{324}s+\frac5{36}-4b
\right].
\]
Thus for a nonzero imaginary interval we need the quadratic
\[
G_b(s)=b^2s^2+\frac{(54b-1)^2}{324}s+\frac5{36}-4b
\]
to be \(\le0\). For fixed \(s\), this is possible only if its discriminant as a quadratic in \(b\) is nonnegative:
\[
\left(\frac{2s}{3}+4\right)^2
-4(s^2+9s)\left(\frac{s}{324}+\frac5{36}\right)\ge0.
\]
After simplifying,
\[
-s^3-18s^2+27s+1296\ge0.
\]
Therefore \(s\le s_*\), where \(s_*\) is the unique positive root of
\[
s^3+18s^2-27s-1296=0.
\]
At equality the corresponding \(b\) is forced:
\[
b=\frac{s_*+6}{3s_*(s_*+9)},
\qquad
a=3b+\frac1{18}.
\]
Writing \(u=s_*+6\), the cubic becomes
\[
u^3-135u-702=0,
\]
so
\[
u=\sqrt[3]{351+54\sqrt{11}}+\sqrt[3]{351-54\sqrt{11}}.
\]
Hence
\[
s_*=\sqrt[3]{351+54\sqrt{11}}
+\sqrt[3]{351-54\sqrt{11}}-6.
\]

The unique maximizing coefficients are
\[
b=\frac{s_*+6}{3s_*(s_*+9)},\qquad
a=\frac{s_*^2+27s_*+108}{18s_*(s_*+9)}.
\]

\[
\boxed{R_*=\sqrt{\sqrt[3]{351+54\sqrt{11}}+\sqrt[3]{351-54\sqrt{11}}-6}}
\]
